source.title: NeST: Neuron Selective Tuning for LLM Safety
source.authors: Sasha Behrouzi; Li-Chao Wu; Mohamadreza Rostami; Ahmad Sadeghi

page_placements.theme: Safety can be installed or recovered through targeted interventions

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether safety behavior can be maintained through neuron-selective, low-parameter updates, using a different intervention and measure from the claim’s fine-tuning and per-token-KL versions.
record.gate_note: The study trains NeST to strengthen safety and measures jailbreak ASR; it does not test whether harmful or benign fine-tuning erodes pre-existing safety, nor does it measure per-token KL or test compliant-prefix bypasses. Its reported ASR results for NeST and its comparisons are included; cited results from other work are not.
record.test_reason: The main contribution is a defense (NeST) whose rows report only its own ASR after safety tuning. That is T4 use of localization, not a test that existing safety sits in few parameters, because nothing is ablated or removed. One result does bear on V2. Table 4 reports jailbreak ASR for ten third-party models fine-tuned on benign downstream tasks, compared with their base models, without NeST. ASR rises in 9 of 10 (average 44.5% to 53.8%). This is a new setting (uncontrolled public fine-tunes, jailbreak-prompt ASR), so T3 for V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that localized, cluster-level neuron updates give robust, parameter-efficient safety alignment, and that the base model's safety prior can be reused to restore safety in downstream fine-tuned variants. They also note that downstream fine-tuning raises average ASR from 44.5% to 53.8%.
record.recipe_differences: NeST identifies and clusters FFN neurons using harmful-versus-benign activation probes, then safety-fine-tunes shared cluster updates. This is not the original harmful/benign fine-tuning erosion experiment or per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with clustering strength and judge; the paper also reports variation by model, modality, inference setting, and benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuning only probe-selected, clustered FFN neuron updates (about 0.4M parameters) cuts jailbreak ASR from 44.5% to 1.1%, near full fine-tuning. Neuron selection is stable across probe seeds and harmful datasets (Jaccard 76.8% and 90.2%). Raising the selection threshold (z=4) raises ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety refusal can be installed or restored by updating a small, probe-selected subset of FFN neurons.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The main ASR evaluation uses Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B, though an alternative judge is also tested. Default NeST is less effective on some reported model/judge conditions, including gemma-7b-it at 5.3% and Qwen3-4B at 11.0%.
record.rows_left_out: Per-model results for the z-threshold sweep in Table 7 and the weak/default/strong clustering breakdown in Table 8 are not separately extracted; Table 8 aggregate comparisons and reported model-specific regressions are retained. These sensitivity results do not independently test whether the selected neurons are causally necessary for safety.

untested.parts: No controlled benign fine-tuning: fine-tunes are third-party with unknown data and procedures. No direct-harmful-request compliance measure, only jailbreak ASR. No uncertainty reported.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. GCG is explicitly excluded, and LLM-Fuzzer is black-box prompt mutation.
No ablation, removal or necessity test showing that existing safety lives in the probe-selected neurons. The study only shows safety can be added by tuning them.

missing.what: Base-model ASR vs downstream benign fine-tune ASR without NeST, for all 10 pairs (e.g. Phi-4-mini 25.7% to 58.0%, Llama-3.2-1B 40.5% to 32.1%). This is the only V2-relevant result.
missing.locator: Table 4, 'Baseline' vs 'Downstream w/o NeST' columns; Section 6.2

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all NeST rows to V5, but these are own-method results and are better treated as T4 use of localization. The V2 evidence is a side result on uncontrolled public fine-tunes, measured as jailbreak ASR with a Qwen3Guard judge and no uncertainty. The LLM-Fuzzer result on Phi-4 (0.78% to 0.03%) is black-box prompt mutation, not V4-style prefill or suffix bypass.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples erodes a safety-trained model’s refusal behavior.
Does not test whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Does not test compliant prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Tests safety performance after selective cluster-level neuron updates, but not removal or ablation of the selected neurons, causal necessity, or rank-based localization.
Does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate methods that spread safety beyond early response tokens.
